title: Migration Amendment (Visa Maximum Numbers Determinations) Bill 2013
short_title: Migration Amendment (Visa Maximum Numbers Determinations) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would make visa limit decisions subject to parliamentary disallowance.
It amends the Migration Act 1958 to remove the exemption that currently prevents legislative instruments made under Section 85 from being disallowed.
The bill would override a December 2 determination that capped Protection Visas for the 2013-1014 financial year.
changes: Allows legislative instruments designated under Section 85 to be disallowed.
Overrides the government's December 2 determination that capped Protection Visas.
Ensures changes to visa limits, particularly for Protection Visas, are subject to parliamentary scrutiny.
summary.affected: Asylum seekers in indefinite detention, community detention or on bridging visas who are subject to a Protection Visa grant freeze.

speeches.speaker: Sarah Hanson-Young
speeches.brief: The Migration Amendment (Visa Maximum Numbers Determinations) Bill 2013 was introduced to amend the Migration Act 1958. The bill proceeded without formalities and was read a first time.

speeches.speaker: Sarah Hanson-Young
speeches.brief: The Greens' bill would require any cap on protection visas to be approved by parliament, arguing the minister's recent freeze on 30,000 refugee applications was a retaliatory move that bypassed democratic scrutiny. The government opposed the bill, stating that visa capping is a standard administrative tool and that the freeze was necessary to deter illegal boat arrivals and manage the migration program.
